question: Which major Indian company was privatised in the 2000s under the Government of India’s disinvestment policy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maruti Udyog Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maruti Udyog Limited**, now known as **Maruti Suzuki India Limited**, was a leading automobile manufacturer in India.
 
• The company was established in **1981** as a joint venture between the **Government of India** and **Suzuki Motor Corporation** of Japan.
 
• Under the **Government of India’s disinvestment policy**, the majority of the government’s stake in Maruti Udyog Limited was sold to Suzuki during the early **2000s**.
 
• The disinvestment process was initiated to **reduce government involvement** in non-strategic sectors, promote private sector efficiency, and generate revenue.
 
• This move marked a significant step in India’s economic liberalization and privatization efforts. **Maruti Udyog Limited** became a wholly owned subsidiary of **Suzuki Motor Corporation**.
 
• The privatization of Maruti Udyog Limited boosted its performance and allowed it to become the leading automobile manufacturer in India.
 
• Other entities mentioned in the options—like **ISRO**, **BSNL**, and **LIC**—are either government organizations or undertakings that were not privatized during the 2000s. *Hence, the correct answer is Maruti Udyog Limited.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maruti Udyog Limited (Maruti Suzuki India Limited):**

 
 
• Founded in **1981**, Maruti Udyog Limited initially focused on producing affordable cars for Indian consumers.
 
• The government held a **74% stake** initially, which was gradually sold to **Suzuki Motor Corporation**, leading to complete privatization.
 
• Maruti Suzuki is known for introducing affordable and fuel-efficient vehicles, such as the **Maruti 800**, which revolutionized the automobile market in India.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment Policy:**
 
 
• The Government of India initiated the **disinvestment policy** in the early **1990s** to reduce its participation in the public sector and promote private sector involvement.
 
• Disinvestment was seen as a way to improve efficiency, reduce the fiscal deficit, and attract foreign investments.
 
• Under this policy, various public sector undertakings were either partially or wholly privatized, depending on their strategic importance.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **ISRO:** The **Indian Space Research Organisation** is a government agency responsible for space research and exploration. It has not been privatized.
 
• **BSNL:** Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited is a state-owned telecommunications company that remains under government ownership.
 
• **LIC:** The Life Insurance Corporation of India is a government-owned insurance corporation and has not been privatized.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Importance of Disinvestment:**

 
 
• Disinvestment helps in reducing the financial burden on the government and improves operational efficiency by involving the private sector.
 
• It also encourages competition, boosts growth, and facilitates technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Other Significant Disinvestments:**
 
 
• Besides Maruti Udyog Limited, notable disinvestments include **Hindustan Zinc**, **Bharat Aluminium Company (BALCO)**, and **VSNL** during the same era.
